patch.value: A binding confined to a block blinds the scan to publishes inside that block

shellScalars refuses every binding not made at file scope, so a binding and the command it routes sit in the same if/for/function/subshell block are never resolved: $CMD publish inside the block is not recognised as a publish at all, and an attested sibling satisfies the non-vacuity guard. Measured: if true; then CMD=npm; $CMD publish; fi returns 0 failures where 1 is required, and a binding two blocks up returns 1 where 0 is required. The fail-open direction (a confined binding attesting a publish outside its block) is already refused; this item is the mirror: refusal must not become blindness.

author: pi-agent
message: Port the five publish-attestation bypass fixes from the pm-todos reference into this repository's own scanner structure

value.note: bindings carry ScalarScope frame serials (control and subshell); scopeEncloses admits only own-or-enclosing frames
four fail-open shapes stay refused; same-block, nested, sibling and subshell mirrors pinned
full suite: bypass 5 fail-open shapes and same-block/nested/sibling/subshell mirrors run with the rest of the scanner suite

patch.value:
Two directions, both measured. The fail-open direction was already refused by this repository's own earlier rounds: an untaken if branch, an else branch, an uncalled function body and a subshell each returned 1 failure before this change (the binding never attests the publish outside it) -- that guard is unchanged. The mirror direction was LIVE: if true; then CMD=npm; $CMD publish; fi returned 0 failures where 1 is required, because the binding was refused outright and the $CMD publish was then not recognised as a publish at all -- the scan was blind, not wrong; and a binding two blocks up returned 1 failure where 0 is required.

Fix, ported from the pm-todos reference into this repository's own structure: the existing scope state machine (control-closer stack, subshell parenthesis counting, multiline function headers, quote and backtick prose) now hands each frame a serial number, so every binding event carries a ScalarScope of open control and subshell frames and every line carries the scope a command on it runs in (closers applied, openers not). scopeEncloses admits an event only from the command's own scope or an enclosing one, so a binding resolves the commands in its block and everything nested in it, and nothing else. A subshell inherits its parent's environment, so outer bindings still attest publishes inside it.

Deliberately stricter than the reference in one measured place: pm-todos resolves by block DEPTH, which cannot tell two sibling blocks apart and credits a later same-depth block with an earlier block's binding. Frame identity refuses that: a binding from a sibling if body or a sibling subshell cannot attest the later block's publish. Both sibling shapes are pinned (1 failure each), so the strictness cannot silently regress either.

Revert-red, both halves: removing the scope filter reddened the new fixture AND five existing guards (unexecuted control flow, nested brace groups, comment syntax scope, phantom scalar-held publish, multiline subshell escape); restoring the old record-only-file-scope behaviour reddened exactly the mirror assertions (same-block 0 failures where 1 required). Restored.

Verified: full suite 361/361 pass; npm run coverage thresholds met at 100/100/100; npm run typecheck; npm run docstring 8 files 55 declarations; npm run verify:release-publish-attestation green over the real workflows; ./node_modules/.bin/pm health --strict-exit exit 0. pm test --run collides with this repository's own pm-integration tests inside the linked-test sandbox (pre-existing, same collision recorded on pm-context-14gn); every linked command was executed directly and observed green, including the single-title run.
Bindings and lines carry frame-serial scopes; scopeEncloses admits own-or-enclosing frames only, keeping in-block resolution while refusing sibling and outward crediting
Confined bindings still refuse outward (4 shapes at 1 failure); same-block, nested and outer-into-subshell bindings resolve (mirrors at 1/0 as measured); siblings stay refused
361/361 tests pass; scope-filter revert reddened the new fixture plus 5 existing guards; record-only-file-scope revert reddened exactly the mirrors; all gates green

value.author: claude
value.text: Verified by behaviour rather than by inspection before committing: this scanner now reports the correct result for all eight known publish-attestation bypasses and for four mirror cases that must keep resolving. The eight are a heredoc body inventing a binding, an escaped separator decoding into scanner syntax, an assignment below a publish resolving it, a backslash-quoted heredoc delimiter that never closed, a binding in an untaken if branch, a nested binding shadowing and then losing an outer one, only the first assignment on a line being recorded, and a binding in an untaken case arm attesting a publish after esac. The last of those was found after this work began and is fixed here anyway. The four mirrors confirm the narrowing did not trade fail-open for fail-silent: a binding in the same block still resolves its command, a binding earlier on the same line still resolves the command after the semicolon, an outer binding still attests a publish nested below it, and a publish inside the case arm that set the flag is still attested. An orphaned history stream named for a descriptive slug rather than an item id was removed rather than committed, since no item file ever existed for it.
